sections.h2: Who handles property tax in McDonald County, Missouri?
sections.html:
Two county offices split the work in McDonald County. The County Assessor values property and handles assessment questions and appeals. The County Collector mails tax statements, takes payment and runs the delinquent tax sale.

  • Collector: 408 Harmon Street, Pineville, MO 64856; mail to PO Box 725; phone (417) 223-7408.
  • Assessor: McDonald County Courthouse, 408 Harmon Street, Pineville; mail to PO Box 726; phone (417) 223-4361 for real estate and mapping.
  • Both offices keep Monday through Friday hours from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, stay open through the noon hour and close on state holidays.

Address changes on a tax bill go through the Assessor, not the Collector. If you are selling and the bill still carries an old mailing address, fix that first.

sections.h2: What is McDonald County like for a seller?
sections.html:
McDonald County fills the far southwestern corner of Missouri. Arkansas lies to the south and Oklahoma to the west, with Newton and Barry counties to the north and east. The county covers 539 square miles of land, was organized in 1849 and has its seat at Pineville. Noel is the largest city, and Anderson, Goodman, Jane, Lanagan and Southwest City are also incorporated communities. Interstate 49 and U.S. 71 carry traffic north and south, and Routes 43, 59, 76 and 90 cover the rest.

The Census Bureau puts the July 2025 population at 23,992, a 3.0 percent rise from the 2020 base. The county has 9,940 housing units, and 67.3 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied. Median value of an owner-occupied home for 2020 to 2024 is $154,700, median gross rent is $767, and median household income is $52,375. The county issued 18 building permits in 2025.

Most of the county sits in the McDonald County R-I School District, headquartered in Anderson, with schools in Noel, Pineville, Rocky Comfort, Southwest City and Jane. Small areas fall in other districts, so the school district line on your tax bill matters when you compare homes.

sections.h2: How does the McDonald County Assessor value a house?
sections.html:
The Assessor values all taxable real and personal property as of January 1, the assessment date set by state statute, and the Missouri State Tax Commission oversees every county assessor's office. The assessed value is a share of market value, and the share depends on the property class.

McDonald County assessment classes with a worked example on $100,000 of market value
Property classAssessment rateAssessed value on $100,000
Residential19%$19,000
Agricultural12%$12,000
Commercial32%$32,000

The levy then comes from each taxing body that covers the parcel: school districts, road districts, cities, fire districts and others such as a junior college. The Assessor's page adds that McDonald County itself receives no property tax levy for operations and relies on sales tax for day to day funding.

Under RSMo 137.115, new assessed values are set on January 1 of each odd-numbered year and carry into the following even year, except new construction. Because 2026 is an even year, the value on your bill this month carries over from the 2025 reassessment, and the next general reassessment date is January 1, 2027. The same section requires a physical inspection before an assessor raises a residential parcel by more than 15 percent, excluding new construction.

sections.h2: When are McDonald County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The Collector mails personal property and real estate statements in the first week of each November. Statements are due on receipt and become delinquent after December 31. For the 2026 bills, that means the mailing is already out and the deadline is December 31, 2026.

  • All statements can be paid with a single check, and partial payment cannot be accepted.
  • Accepted payment types are cash, personal check, money order and credit card, in person, by mail or online.
  • Payments postmarked after December 31 are returned unprocessed unless late fees are included.
  • If no statement arrives by the end of November, call the Collector. Not receiving a bill does not erase the obligation or any penalty and interest.

Missouri law has the collector add a penalty once taxes go unpaid past the delinquency date (RSMo 139.100). Ask the Collector at (417) 223-7408 for the current penalty and interest percentages before you pay late. The same statute treats a mailed payment as paid on its postmark date.

The Collector also holds the delinquent tax sale in August each year, so a parcel with old unpaid bills can move toward auction long before a seller notices.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a McDonald County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the Assessor. Call (417) 223-4361 and ask for an informal review of the value, bringing sales of similar nearby homes, repair estimates or photos that support a lower number. Ask the same office for the filing date of the county Board of Equalization.

If the board leaves the value unchanged, RSMo 138.430 lets an owner appeal to the State Tax Commission within the time set by statute or thirty days after the board's final action, whichever is later. When an appeal is filed, the disputed taxes are impounded in a separate fund instead of going to the taxing bodies.

Missouri also lets a taxpayer pay under protest. Under RSMo 139.031, you pay the full bill before the delinquency date and file a written statement of your grounds with the collector. A protest that is not followed by a circuit court suit against the collector within ninety days becomes void. An appeal already pending before the State Tax Commission replaces that suit requirement.

sections.h2: What relief programs apply to McDonald County owners?
sections.html:
The Missouri Department of Revenue runs the Property Tax Credit Claim, often called the circuit breaker. It gives certain senior citizens and 100 percent disabled individuals a credit for part of the real estate tax or rent paid, up to $1,100 for owners who own and occupy their home and $750 for renters. The amount depends on taxes paid and total household income, taxable and nontaxable. Questions go to PropertyTaxCredit@dor.mo.gov.

The State Tax Commission also explains a homestead exemption for a former prisoner of war who has a total service-connected disability. The owner must occupy the homestead as a primary residence and give the assessor proof, including a letter from the Department of Veterans Affairs and discharge records or a records center letter showing former prisoner of war status.

Military personnel stationed in the county under orders with a home of record outside Missouri generally do not owe Missouri personal property tax on non-business items, according to the same State Tax Commission FAQ.

sections.h2: What should a McDonald County seller do about unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Treat the tax bill as a closing item. Before listing a McDonald County house, call the Collector to learn the status of every year on the parcel, then ask the closing agent to prorate the current year between buyer and seller. A parcel with delinquent years can reach the August sale, so clear older balances first.

  • Confirm the owner name and mailing address with the Assessor.
  • Ask the Collector for a balance on each parcel you are selling, including land and any manufactured home.
  • Keep your settlement statement, because it shows how the year's tax was split.
  • If the assessed value looks high, raise it with the Assessor before the board deadline rather than after closing.

faqs.q: When do McDonald County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: After December 31. Statements are mailed in the first week of November and are due on receipt, and payments postmarked after December 31 are returned unless late fees are included.

faqs.q: Can I pay half of my McDonald County bill now and half later?
faqs.a: No. The Collector states that partial payment cannot be accepted, though all statements can be paid together with one check.

faqs.q: What percentage of value is a McDonald County home assessed at?
faqs.a: Residential property is assessed at 19 percent of market value, agricultural at 12 percent and commercial at 32 percent. A $100,000 home therefore carries an assessed value of $19,000 before the levy is applied.

faqs.q: Who do I call to change the address on my McDonald County tax statement?
faqs.a: The County Assessor's Office at (417) 223-4361. The Collector's site says address changes go through the Assessor.

faqs.q: When is the McDonald County delinquent tax sale?
faqs.a: The Collector holds the delinquent tax sale in August. Call the Collector at (417) 223-7408 for the exact date and the parcels listed.
